rows.exactQuestion: By what form is the Illinois mistaken-identity petition under 20 ILCS 2630/5.2 verified: (a) an unsworn certification by the participant under 735 ILCS 5/1-109, or (b) an affidavit sworn before a notary with a jurat? The committed record names the instrument a 'Verified petition' but nowhere states which of the two it takes, and the two impose materially different burdens on the participant - (a) is self-executing at the kitchen table, (b) requires personal appearance before a notary. Composing either one would be this lane choosing the legal form, which the assignment forbids.
rows.whyNotAnsweredByInference: 735 ILCS 5/1-109 is a general Illinois certification provision, so it is tempting to treat it as the default for any pleading called verified. This lane did not, because in the held Illinois record 1-109 is never a default: it attaches to specific official forms that carry the verification on their own face. Every one of the nine 1-109 citations in IL.memo.json is the Application for Waiver of Court Fees signatory, and the only other 1-109 use in the repository, scripts/build-census-v1-il-exp-pardon-set.mjs, is the participant signing the official statewide EXP-AD Request. This family renders no official form at all - custodyClass CUSTOM_PLEADING_FROM_CODIFIED_TEXT, sourceBinaryCommitted false - so the mechanism that carries 1-109 in every recorded Illinois instance is absent here, and the inference does not transfer.
